title: Intermittent token rejections after an afternoon of changes
context: A SaaS product's API gateway verifies JWT access tokens issued by auth-service. Public verification keys are cached on each gateway node by a jwks-agent daemon that the gateway pods read from. On Sep 21 at 14:05 UTC users began to be logged out intermittently. The investigation proceeded in three stages; evidence is labelled with the stage at which it became available. Some scored items ask for the state that was warranted at a particular stage.

entities.description: 24 gateway pods that verify JWT signatures and time claims.
Per-node daemon that fetches and caches the JWKS public keys for gateway pods on that node.
Token issuer; three replicas (auth-1, auth-2, auth-3) behind a round-robin load balancer.
Publishes the public keys that the gateway uses to verify token signatures.
Controller that delivers signing-key material to auth-service replicas.

evidence.text: HTTP 401 responses are 3.1% of authenticated API requests since 14:05 (baseline 0.3%). Both web and mobile users report being logged out unexpectedly.
Gateway v2.8 was rolled out to all 24 gateway pods between 13:50 and 14:00. Its changelog includes a JWT library upgrade from 4.2 to 5.0.

Weekly signing-key rotation: new key K2 was published on the JWKS endpoint alongside K1 at 13:30, and auth-service replicas switched to signing with K2 at 14:00. The rotation has run weekly for 20 weeks without incident.
Clock-offset alarm at 14:10: three of the twelve gateway nodes were 1.2-1.8 s ahead of reference time.
Mobile app v7.1 was released to 10% of mobile users at 12:00 on Sep 21.
12 of the 24 gateway pods were rolled back to v2.7 at 14:45. From 14:45 to 15:05 the 401 rate was 3.0% on v2.7 pods and 3.2% on v2.8 pods.

401s are spread evenly across pods (2.8-3.4% each), including pods on the three nodes with clock offset. Rejection reasons: 98% 'signature verification failed', 2% 'token expired', none 'token not yet valid'. The gateway allows 30 s of clock leeway.
Of 200 rejected tokens sampled at 15:00, all carry key ID K2.

evidence.source: gateway debug dumps posted in incident channel (14:52)
evidence.text: Two dumps labelled 'gw-prod-node-3 jwks-agent' and 'gw-prod-node-7 jwks-agent': each cached key set contains only K1, with last JWKS fetch at 13:12. Configured scheduled refresh interval: 24 hours.
All three auth-service replicas report healthy. Token issuance rate is normal.

Both 14:52 dumps were taken from jwks-agents on staging nodes (gw-staging-node-3 and gw-staging-node-7); the production labels were a copy-paste error. Dumps from jwks-agents on four production gateway nodes at 15:20 show K1 and K2, with K2 received at 13:31 through auth-service's key-publication push. Staging jwks-agents are not subscribed to publication pushes.
Of 1,000 accepted tokens sampled at 15:30, 310 carry key ID K2.

Token ID prefixes identify the issuing replica. All 200 rejected tokens from the 15:00 sample and 500 further rejected tokens sampled at 15:30 were issued by auth-2. The accepted K2 tokens were issued by auth-1 and auth-3.
Offline verification of auth-2-issued K2 tokens against the published K2 public key fails. The fingerprint of the K2 private key mounted on auth-2 differs from the one mounted on auth-1 and auth-3.

auth-2 runs in a different availability zone; its secret volume was last updated at 13:58. secret-sync logs for 13:30-14:00 have been rotated out, and there is no record of what material was delivered to auth-2 or whether the mounted file was changed by other means.

hypotheses.text: The JWT library upgrade in gateway v2.8 causes the gateway to reject valid tokens.
Production gateway nodes are verifying with a cached key set that lacks K2.
Gateway clock offset causes valid tokens to be rejected.
An auth-service replica is signing tokens with key material that does not match the published key.
secret-sync delivered incorrect K2 key material to auth-2.

edges.from: clock offset on three gateway nodes

actions.text: Roll 12 of the 24 gateway pods back to v2.7 and compare 401 rates between versions.
Force an immediate JWKS refresh on the jwks-agents of all production gateway nodes.
Remove auth-2 from the auth-service load balancer until its K2 key material is replaced.
Roll back the key rotation: return all replicas to signing with K1 and remove K2 from the JWKS endpoint.
Roll the remaining gateway pods back to v2.7.
Shorten the jwks-agent scheduled refresh interval from 24 hours to 5 minutes on all gateway nodes.
